entrypoints.summary: LockToVote.vote is callable by a caller passing auth(LOCK_MANAGER_PERMISSION_ID), without the reported pre-fix check that the caller is the configured LockManager.
LockToVote.clearVote is likewise reported to authorize through LOCK_MANAGER_PERMISSION_ID without validating that msg.sender is the configured LockManager.

affected_components.role: Reported pre-fix authorization entrypoints and context locations L148 and L211; report also cites L28.

negative_controls: A caller that is not the configured LockManager is rejected after the reported identity requirement is applied.
No execution trace or test result is supplied to confirm either control.
observability.positive_marker: A proposal's vote accounting or success/failure outcome reflects forged voting power or an unauthorized cleared vote.

preconditions: The caller holds LOCK_MANAGER_PERMISSION_ID but is not the configured LockManager.
The report describes the affected vote or clearVote authorization behavior; no supplied transaction artifact establishes a practical setup for obtaining this permission.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A vote request originating from a non-manager permission holder with a chosen voter identity and voting-power amount.
trigger_steps.summary: Invoke vote while supplying an arbitrary address and arbitrary claimed voting power, exploiting acceptance of a permission holder in place of the LockManager.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A clear-vote request from a non-manager permission holder directed at an existing vote.
trigger_steps.summary: Alternatively invoke clearVote to remove an existing voter's vote without that voter's consent.

relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that an entity with the permission but not acting as LockManager can vote on behalf of any address with arbitrary voting power.
The report says arbitrary unbacked voting power lets the entity decide proposal success or failure.
The report says arbitrary clearing of an existing vote can freely decide proposal success or failure.
The reported PR 39 change adds msg.sender == address(lockManager) to vote; the same identity requirement is reported for clearVote.

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of LockToVote governance proposal outcomes and vote records
impact.attacker_capability: A non-LockManager holder of LOCK_MANAGER_PERMISSION_ID can vote for arbitrary addresses using arbitrary voting power without locking tokens, or clear an existing vote.
impact.security_effect: Governance vote accounting can be forged or erased, which the report says permits deciding proposal success or failure.

causal_trace.summary: An entity other than the configured LockManager holds LOCK_MANAGER_PERMISSION_ID and invokes vote or clearVote.

Role authorization is accepted in place of the designated LockManager's identity, although that manager is the component that supplies the voter identity and amount of locked voting power to the plugin.
vote processes externally supplied voter and voting-power information without requiring msg.sender == address(lockManager); clearVote can similarly process a non-manager caller's clearing request.

The report states that the permission holder can cast a vote for any address with arbitrary voting power without token transfer or locking, or clear an existing voter's vote, thereby deciding proposal success or failure.

failure.operation: Acceptance of a permission-holder's vote or vote-clear request as a LockManager-originated accounting attestation

primary_invariant.statement: Only the configured LockManager may attest locked voting power and submit or clear votes in LockToVotePlugin.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The affected functions reportedly accepted any caller with LOCK_MANAGER_PERMISSION_ID but did not verify that msg.sender equaled address(lockManager).

provenance.source_id: Spearbit Aragon DAO Gov Plugin Security Review, finding 5.3.5

quality.review_notes: Finding-level report prose directly describes the pre-fix authorization path, impacts, and PR 39 changes. The bundle contains no source snapshot, PR diff, test, transaction trace, or execution result; PR 39 is only report-described, so remediation and exploitability are not independently code- or execution-verified.

remediation.invariant_restored: vote and clearVote require msg.sender == address(lockManager), restoring the configured manager as the sole vote-accounting attestor.
